_meta.purpose: Manual override surface for slide images. Edit a value here, re-run npm run build:lessons (TODO: implement), and the new image will appear in the slide.

gravitation-1.alt: Two masses separated by a distance r, with attractive force arrows along the line joining their centers
gravitation-1.caption: Two masses attract each other along the line joining their centers.

gravitation-2.alt: Diagram showing field lines around a massive object weakening with distance
gravitation-2.caption: Field lines spread out as you move away — the field strength drops as 1/r².

gravitation-3.alt: A satellite orbiting Earth in a circular path, with the radius r marked from Earth's center
gravitation-3.caption: The farther the orbit, the slower the satellite moves.

projectile-motion-1.alt: A basketball following a parabolic arc toward a hoop
projectile-motion-1.caption: The trajectory of a projectile is a parabola under gravity alone.

projectile-motion-2.alt: A ball falling straight down with velocity vectors shown at equal time intervals
projectile-motion-2.caption: Equal time steps — the distance between snapshots grows because v_y grows.

projectile-motion-3.alt: A projectile launched at an angle with its velocity vector split into horizontal and vertical components
projectile-motion-3.caption: Horizontal and vertical motion are independent but share the same flight time.

relative-velocity-1.alt: A person walking forward on a moving bus, with velocity arrows shown from two different observers
relative-velocity-1.caption: Two observers, two different answers — both correct, in their own frame.

relative-velocity-2.alt: A student walking on a bus with velocity arrows for the bus and the student
relative-velocity-2.caption: Same direction → add. Opposite direction → subtract.

relative-velocity-3.alt: A boat crossing a river with the current shown as a separate vector
relative-velocity-3.caption: Boat velocity and current velocity add as vectors, not as plain numbers.

describing-rotation-1.alt: A circle with the radius r, arc length s, and angle θ marked at the center
describing-rotation-1.caption: θ = s / r — the radius and the arc it sweeps define the angle.

describing-rotation-2.alt: A spinning disc with angular velocity and angular acceleration arrows at the center
describing-rotation-2.caption: ω tells you how fast it spins; α tells you how fast that spin rate is changing.

describing-rotation-3.alt: A rotating wheel with two marked points — one near the center, one on the rim
describing-rotation-3.caption: Same angular speed, very different linear speeds at different radii.

rotational-dynamics-1.alt: A door with a force vector applied at the edge, perpendicular to the door, with the lever arm r marked
rotational-dynamics-1.caption: The longer the lever arm, the greater the torque for the same push.

rotational-dynamics-2.alt: Two objects of equal mass — a long rod and a compact disk — about different axes of rotation
rotational-dynamics-2.caption: Same mass, different moment of inertia — it is the distribution that matters.

rotational-dynamics-3.alt: An ice skater in two positions — arms extended and arms pulled in
rotational-dynamics-3.caption: Pulling mass inward drops I, so ω must rise to keep L constant.

impulse-momentum-1.alt: Two moving objects with different masses and velocities, momentum vectors shown
impulse-momentum-1.caption: Momentum points the same way as velocity — it is a vector quantity.

impulse-momentum-2.alt: A baseball being struck by a bat, with the contact force and contact time indicated
impulse-momentum-2.caption: The bat delivers a large impulse over a very short contact time.

impulse-momentum-3.alt: A force-time graph with a clear peak, the area under the curve shaded
impulse-momentum-3.caption: The shaded area under an F–t graph is the impulse delivered.

conservation-momentum-1.alt: Two carts about to collide on a low-friction track, momentum vectors shown
conservation-momentum-1.caption: Internal forces between the carts cannot change the total momentum.

conservation-momentum-2.alt: Two carts colliding and sticking together, before and after the collision
conservation-momentum-2.caption: Momentum is conserved; kinetic energy is not.

conservation-momentum-3.alt: A rifle firing a bullet, with the bullet moving forward and the rifle recoiling backward
conservation-momentum-3.caption: Equal and opposite momenta — the gun kicks back as the bullet flies forward.

work-energy-1.alt: A person pushing a crate along the floor with the force vector at an angle to the displacement
work-energy-1.caption: Only the component of F along d contributes to the work.

work-energy-2.alt: A moving vehicle with its kinetic energy indicated as dependent on mass and speed squared
work-energy-2.caption: Energy grows with v² — small speed changes make a big difference.

work-energy-3.alt: Two light bulbs with different wattages, illustrating different power ratings
work-energy-3.caption: Higher wattage means the same energy in less time.

energy-conservation-1.alt: A collage of energy forms — motion, heat, light, electricity, sound
energy-conservation-1.caption: All these everyday phenomena are energy transforming from one form to another.

energy-conservation-2.alt: A ball held at height h above the ground, with gravitational potential energy indicated
energy-conservation-2.caption: PE depends on height above your chosen reference level.

energy-conservation-3.alt: A roller coaster with positions marked where gravitational PE is high and where KE is high
energy-conservation-3.caption: High point → mostly PE. Low point → mostly KE. Total stays the same.
